mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (1-month change in FEDFUNDS < 0) signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods with negative FEDFUNDS change are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in CPIAUCSL exceeding 0.5% (relative to prior month) signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month, or the average return in such instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both employment growth (PAYEMS) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) exceed 0.3% monthly growth, it indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.3% and RSAFS growth > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in > 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and RSAFS growth exceed 0.3% in 1 month, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate (1-month change < -0.1%) signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0% and UNRATE falls > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0% and UNRATE falls > 0.1% in 1 month, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly reading of industrial production (INDPRO) above 115 signals strong manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO > 115, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) both show monthly growth exceeding 0.2%, it indicates robust economic momentum that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 0.2% and HOUST growth > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in > 60% of instances where both INDPRO and HOUST growth exceed 0.2% in 1 month, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals a tight labor market that may trigger inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) reading above 1800 thousand units signals robust consumer demand for housing, which supports economic expansion and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 1800, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
